events.text: On the highest ground your life will ever reach, the wind drops. A seam opens in the evening light, and out of it, one at a time, step the lives you have lived. None of them looks like you. Every one regards you as a reader regards the last leaf of a long book.

effects.log: You wait, hands loose at your sides. The first of them steps forward.
"I know you," you say, and it is true. The first of them smiles and steps forward.

events.text: {pst_Name} steps out of the dusk: {pst_what}. They walk once around you, reading what their road became after they left it. "So that is where it led," {pst_name} says. "I did wonder."

effects.log: You offer your open hand and ask. The question hangs between you in the cooling air.
You take them as they were, faults and all. They come into you without a word.

choices.text: Thank them, and let them go

effects.log: You thank them for the road. They walk back into the dusk, lighter.

events.text: {pst_Name} comes out of the evening: {pst_what}. They remember a summit like this one, and a life of yours that stood on it and turned them away. "You refused us once," {pst_name} says. "We have wondered whether you were sure."

choices.text: Ask them again to join you

effects.log: You ask, and this time you mean every word.
You do not ask. You simply take them back, and they allow it.

choices.text: Tell them you were sure, and let them go

effects.log: You were sure. They nod, as if you had confirmed an old suspicion, and fade.

events.text: From the long grass comes {pst_name}, {pst_what}, vast and unhurried, smelling of rain on warm stone. It lowers its head until one eye is level with yours. It never could speak. It waits only to learn whether you remember.

choices.text: Lay a hand on its brow and ask

effects.log: You rest your palm on its brow and ask without words. Its breath is warm on your wrist.
You wrap your arms around as much of it as you can reach. It makes the sound it made when it was content.

choices.text: Bow to it, and let it go

effects.log: You bow low. It turns, slow as a hillside, and walks back into the grass.

events.text: {pst_Name} walks out in the cloak of {pst_what}, and the whole valley seems to stand straighter. "I wore a crown," the old king says. "You wear a name. Persuade me that is worth more."

effects.log: You make it as one ruler to another, plainly, without raising your voice.

choices.text: Kneel and take the king back

effects.log: You kneel. The king lifts you up, and the cloak settles on your shoulders and is gone.

choices.text: Say the crown is finished, and let them go

effects.log: The king looks at you a long while, then laughs, and the laugh goes on after the king has gone.

events.text: Last of them, and slowest, comes {pst_name}: {pst_what}. They sit on a stone as if the summit were theirs, still smiling. "The rest came to weigh you," they say. "I came to find out how long you will keep pretending we are strangers."

choices.text: Ask them to join you, on your terms

effects.log: You ask, on your terms, and wait. They seem to find the terms amusing.
You take them back, shadow and all. It is heavier than you thought, and it is yours.

choices.text: Refuse to carry them, and let them go

effects.log: You let them go. They shrug, smiling still, and the dusk takes them.

events.text: Your past selves stand about you on the summit, the ones who came close nearest, the rest farther off, all waiting. Take every one back into a single self, or only some, or thank them and stay as you are. The answer is yours, and none of them will hurry you.

effects.log: You breathe. There is no hurry on the highest ground.

choices.text: Look at each face in turn

effects.log: You look at every face, and every face looks back. The answer is coming.

events.text: The selves who joined you are part of you now: their years, their strength, their old griefs grown calm. The ones who did not stand a little apart at the edge of the light, and you understand they will remember this. Then the dusk takes them, and it is only you again. Larger.

choices.text: Thank the ones who stayed apart

effects.log: You thank them across the distance. One of them lifts a hand.
You walk down. There is still a life to live, even here.

events.text: "I am this one," you said, and they heard. They do not argue. Each touches your shoulder as they pass, the way travellers touch a waymark, and files back into the dusk. The last turns at the edge. "We will remember you said that," they say. It sounds like a blessing.

effects.log: You bow until they are gone. You are only yourself. It is enough.
You laugh, a little, on the highest ground. It is a very human sound up here.

events.text: Last night you dreamed of a procession over a ridge that was not a ridge, every walker laying a hand on your shoulder in passing. You wake sure of one thing and unable to say why: somewhere, once, you chose to remain yourself, and they let you.

effects.log: Whatever this life becomes, it will be yours. The thought is very steadying.
You wonder all day. By evening the faces are gone, and the certainty is not.

events.text: Some mornings you know things nobody taught you: how a hawk sleeps, how a crown sits, how an old harvest song goes. The village teacher calls you an old soul. You privately suspect you are several, and that a few of them are still waiting.

choices.text: Listen for the ones who wait

effects.log: You listen. Very far off, someone is still standing at the edge of the light.

choices.text: Be grateful for the ones who came

effects.log: You are grateful. The harvest song stays in your head all day.
